title: Google Vids now lets you star in your own AI videos
slides: Google Vids lets you insert yourself into AI clips. Why?
It uses a single selfie to map your face onto scenes.
But your expressions stay frozen while the background moves.
You can now narrate a presentation with your avatar instantly.
Test it today: see if your team spots the uncanny part.
thread_text:
1. Your face, their puppet

Google Vids only needs one selfie to transfer your likeness into a video scene. No movement required from you.

2. The frozen smile problem

Your expressions remain locked the entire time while the background scenery shifts around you. It's a face, not a performance.

3. The instant narrator trick

You can generate a full presentation avatar in seconds. No recording studio, no retakes, just a single photo.

4. The uncanny gap

Your team will likely notice something off. The mismatch between a still face and moving background creates an eerie effect.

5. Spot the flaw this week

Test it on one internal video today. Ask three colleagues to watch — does anyone notice the frozen face before you point it out?
video_script: One selfie is all they need.
Can your team spot the glitch?
